identity.name: Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia
identity.wikipedia: Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia

land.text: the Serbian core of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, which 'Germany occupied ... outright and placed ... under direct military administration' after the surrender of 17 April 1941

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Serbia row has only one shape, a 66-cell patch of Vardar Macedonia in 1918 (the eu-21 serbia dossier); it does not cover 1941-1944.

land.text: 'Most of Serbia was liberated from the Germans over the course of the Belgrade Offensive'; Red Army 'took the city on 20 October' 1944

successors.note: Partisans and the Red Army; the land becomes part of the new Yugoslavia (socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia, eu-22).

rulers.name: Milan Nedić
rulers.title: Head of the Government of National Salvation (Serbian puppet government under the German Military Commander)
rulers.note: 'Puppet regime established: 29 August 1941', 'the Government of National Salvation under Serbian general Milan Nedić'. The page gives his start, not his end; the real authority was the German Military Commander (Helmuth Förster April-June 1941, Paul Bader 1941-1943 on the infobox).

correction.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no shape for occupied Serbia (its Serbia row is one 1918 patch of Vardar Macedonia). The page gives no area (page silent), only 'Population 1941: 4,500,000'; the resolved spec is the page's 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat'. The page does not name the Bulgarian cut (Pirot is read from 'parts of eastern Serbia' on the Axis occupation page) and says 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included in the occupied territory' before the border moved after pressure from the NDH, undated. The Banat was 'an autonomous region throughout the occupation', governed by its Volksdeutsche minority, and is kept inside the shape.

region.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

ledger.note: 22 April 1941: German Military Commander takes charge of occupied Serbia. 'On 22 April 1941, the Territory was placed under the supreme authority of the German Military Commander in Serbia'; infobox 'Occupation started: 22 April 1941'. Yugoslavia had surrendered on 17 April 1941 (Axis occupation page).

region.text: Serbia under direct German military administration

ledger.note: 22 April 1941: Germany rules Serbia directly. 'Germany occupied Serbia outright and placed it under direct military administration'; the nazi-germany dossier records the same land as occupation of Yugoslavia.

region.text: the Republic of Užice, bounded by the Valjevo–Bajina Bašta line to the north, the Drina to the west, the Zapadna Morava to the east and the Raška region to the south (the page's description); 15,000-20,000 km2 on the Užice page, read as the Zlatibor, Moravica and Raška districts

ledger.note: 28 July 1941: the Partisans enter Užice and found the Republic of Užice. Infobox 'Partisan arrival in Užice: 28 July 1941'; the Territory page: 'In early July 1941, shortly after the launching of Operation Barbarossa, armed resistance began'; the Užice page gives 15,000 or 20,000 km2.

29 August 1941: Serbia gets a puppet government. 'Puppet regime established: 29 August 1941'; 'the Government of National Salvation under Serbian general Milan Nedić'. The Military Commander stays the real authority.

region.text: the Republic of Užice, bounded by the Valjevo–Bajina Bašta line to the north, the Drina to the west, the Zapadna Morava to the east and the Raška region to the south (the page's description); 15,000-20,000 km2 on the Užice page, read as the Zlatibor, Moravica and Raška districts

ledger.note: 1 December 1941: the Germans reconquer the Republic of Užice. Infobox 'Conquered: 1 December 1941'; 'In November 1941, in the First anti-Partisan offensive, the German troops occupied this territory again'; the Territory page dates the German expulsion to 'late September 1941' (Operation Uzice), which conflicts. 'At the beginning of December 1941 the partisans moved from Serbia to Bosnia'.

region.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

ledger.note: October 1944: the Red Army and the Partisans take Serbia. 'The Red Army organised the Belgrade Offensive, and took the city on 20 October'; 'Most of Serbia was liberated from the Germans over the course of the Belgrade Offensive' (Territory page).

region.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

ledger.note: October 1944: the German administration leaves. 'the administration was evacuated from Serbia to Vienna in October 1944'; infobox 'Territory liberated: 20 October 1944'.

region.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

ledger.note: 20 October 1944: the Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia ends. 'The Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia dissolved in 1944, when Germans withdrew in the face of a combined' Soviet-Partisan offensive (the extract of the sentence ends there).

wars.name: Invasion of Yugoslavia

zones.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

wars.outcome: Germany, Italy and Hungary invaded Yugoslavia on 6 April 1941; the unconditional surrender was signed on 17 April 1941 and Germany occupied Serbia outright under direct military administration on 22 April.
wars.note: The Invasion of Yugoslavia article was not opened (page budget); the dates are from the Axis occupation page, which says Germany, Italy and Hungary invaded (Bulgaria moved in on 19 April).

wars.name: First anti-Partisan offensive

zones.text: the Republic of Užice, bounded by the Valjevo–Bajina Bašta line to the north, the Drina to the west, the Zapadna Morava to the east and the Raška region to the south (the page's description); 15,000-20,000 km2 on the Užice page, read as the Zlatibor, Moravica and Raška districts

wars.outcome: German troops reconquer the Republic of Užice (conquered 1 December 1941); the Partisans withdraw to Bosnia, Sandžak and Montenegro.
wars.note: The Territory page calls the same fighting 'Operation Uzice' and dates its launch 'late September 1941'; the Užice page says the offensive was in November 1941. Disagreement not resolved.

wars.name: Belgrade offensive

zones.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

wars.outcome: The Red Army and the Partisans take Belgrade on 20 October 1944; the German administration is evacuated to Vienna and the Territory ends.

certainty.note: The pages name the Territory's parts (central Serbia, the Banat, north Kosovo) but not its borders with the Bulgarian, Hungarian and Croatian zones, which moved (eastern Syrmia was 'initially included'); the border with Montenegro is not described.

sources.title: Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia
sources.note: Identity, 22 April 1941, territory read as central Serbia, Banat and north Kosovo, Nedić regime 29 August 1941, end October 1944. No area figure.

sources.title: Axis occupation of Yugoslavia
sources.note: Invasion 6 April and surrender 17 April 1941, partition among Germany, Italy, Hungary, Bulgaria and the NDH, Belgrade offensive 20 October 1944. Silent on Montenegro's declaration and on Pirot.

sources.title: Republic of Užice
sources.note: Partisan arrival 28 July 1941, conquest 1 December 1941, 15,000-20,000 km2, boundaries.

notes: Cliopatria's only Serbia shape is the 1918 Macedonian-front patch (serbia dossier). Pages are silent on: the Bulgarian annexation of the Pirot area (the Axis page says only 'parts of eastern Serbia' on 19 April and 'formally annexed' 14 May), the date and extent of the Syrmian border change, and the Sandžak. The two pages disagree on the German operation against the Partisans (Operation Uzice, late September 1941, on the Territory page; First anti-Partisan offensive, November 1941, on the Užice page). Montenegro under Italian and then German rule needs its own dossier (the Axis occupation page says only that Italy 'gained control over Montenegro' and, after 8 September 1943, 'The former Italian kingdoms of Albania and of Montenegro were placed under German occupation'): counterparts_needing_dossiers 'Italian Governorate of Montenegro'. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none (the district names of Serbia and the Kosovo municipalities resolve).
